approved: New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2024
Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications and the Arts
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record

This bill is part of a package that would create a new vehicle efficiency standard for Australia, reducing carbon dioxide emissions from new cars and light commercial vehicles and boosting the supply of low and zero emission vehicles.

The standard would set annual emissions targets for suppliers, who would earn credits for beating them and face penalties for exceeding them, with the ability to trade credits and a two-year grace period to comply.
The package would amend the Clean Energy Regulator Act 2011 and the Road Vehicle Standards Act 2018 to support the new framework, and the bill includes a review of the scheme in 2026.
Establishes a new vehicle efficiency standard for Australia.
Sets CO2 emissions targets for each regulated year from 2025 to 2029.
Allows suppliers to earn and trade credits for exceeding targets.
Imposes civil penalties for suppliers whose emissions remain above target after the grace period.
Enables the Minister to set targets for later years via legislative instrument.
Triggers the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014 for enforcement.
Vehicle suppliers bringing new cars, SUVs, utes, and vans to the Australian market.

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2024-05-16.17.2): > *That so much of the standing orders be suspended as would prevent the motion of the third reading being moved without delay.* Standing orders are the usual procedural rules of parliament. This vote is to allow the ordinary process of considering bills to be hurried along.
